reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that thermal aging at 700°C in a TiVNbTa RHEA causes trace interstitials to promote phase segregation and precipitate formation, but it does not address the effects of cyclic mechanical loading, grain-boundary segregation, or the link to brittle fracture and toughness loss. The key premises involving stress-driven diffusion, grain-boundary segregation, and the resulting brittle fracture mechanism are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Cyclic loading at 700°C accelerates atomic diffusion in single-phase HEAs
Trace interstitials or solute elements segregate to grain boundaries under these conditions
Segregation leads to nucleation of nanoscale brittle precipitates at grain boundaries
These precipitates reduce intergranular cohesion and act as stress concentrators
The microstructural change causes a transition from ductile to brittle fracture with reduced toughness
